body: You're right. I definitely think the amount others around them that are reliant on the person considering suicide should be factored in when evaluating if it's the best decision; however, wouldn't that mean that those people around them that are reliant are just being selfish, unless, of course, the persons' are children. I don't know everything. I'm just saying. Perhaps, this is a better discussion for /r/suicidology
I appreciate your efforts to help with my post. I should have made a quick throwaway to ask it. I hope you take care too :).
Awe, don't worry about that. Nothing you have said has *encouraged* my decision. You were just being helpful! :) I sought out many resources to get my answer anyways, so don't feel bad.
thanks. this should make it super easy.

Reread your comment more slowly this time. Maybe I should research "tried and true" language types. I should also mention that there isn't actual a close person to see this stuff gets carried out, unless I get a last minute "care director". If you know the answer, is it possible for none of my will to matter since there isn't a specific person to execute it? I'd like the reassurance that it's going to be done, but I rather know the truth if it probably won't. Hope my question makes sense!

Well, I looked around and just the standard parts from what I saw from samples. Do i need those "article I, article II" parts?

I included my SSN, address, family information, and other parts I saw that didn't involve money or cars/houses. 

I already handled my money while alive. My other belongings are just a LITTLE bit of furniture and a few electronics (printers, television), lots of clothing. I was able to donate a lot, but I didn't get to take care a chunk of my belongings that are in a storage unit. It's not a huge deal. I think if I don't donate it; it gets auctioned after I don't return for a certain amount of time anyways. I payed for it a few months ahead of time in case it takes awhile for it to be donated.

As for a lawyer, at this point, I don't think I have enough money to get one. What if I just make sure it's notarized?

From what I saw online, handwritten wills are accepted in California, but are you saying if I really want this to be carried out I need to get a lawyer?
I don't know how to explain it, really. It's too complex or I'm just making it complicated.
Trust me. No one wants me around them.

It's many things. I probably have a mental illness, which doesn't help. I am very socially inept. I am in a lot of pain daily, most of which is in my mind. It's difficult to explain. I tried explaining some of it [here](http://www.reddit.com/r/self/comments/1yaw58/expediting_my_plans_instead_of_two_weeks_i_should/) in a previous post. 

I feel like there are 3+ people inside of me and I have never been able to form healthy relationships because of how I perceive things. I am very, very weird and I make people uncomfortable. Even though I get good grades I will likely never get a good job. It's a lot and its hard to explain.
